subtopics.name: Upper GI disorders and GI bleeding

questions.stem: Highlight the findings that require immediate follow-up.

cells: Sudden tearing pain through to the back, 10 of 10
Right arm 196/104, left arm 150/88 mm Hg

rationale.correct: Tearing back pain, unequal arm pressures, a new aortic murmur and a wide mediastinum are the cues of dissection.

perOption.r1: Sudden tearing pain radiating to the back is the classic description of aortic dissection.
perOption.r2: A difference of more than 20 mm Hg between the arms means the tear is affecting a branch artery.
perOption.r3: A new diastolic murmur suggests aortic regurgitation from a dissection reaching the aortic valve.
perOption.r4: A widened mediastinum supports dissection of the thoracic aorta.
perOption.r5: Expected with pain; the absence of ST elevation helps rule out STEMI but is not itself a problem.

questions.educationalObjective: Recognize cues of aortic dissection.

questions.stem: For each finding, indicate the condition or conditions it can be consistent with. Each row may have more than one answer.

rows.text: Sudden severe chest pain
Blood pressure difference of more than 20 mm Hg between the arms
Widened mediastinum on chest x-ray
Raised D-dimer
ST elevation in two adjacent leads
Pleuritic pain with low oxygen saturation

rationale.correct: The findings specific to dissection are unequal arm pressures, a wide mediastinum and a new aortic murmur; pain and D-dimer overlap with MI and PE.

perOption.r1:c1: All three cause sudden chest pain, so pain alone does not separate them.
perOption.r1:c2: All three cause sudden chest pain, so pain alone does not separate them.
perOption.r1:c3: All three cause sudden chest pain, so pain alone does not separate them.
perOption.r2:c1: Unequal pressures come from the tear narrowing a subclavian artery.
perOption.r2:c2: Unequal pressures come from the tear narrowing a subclavian artery.
perOption.r2:c3: Unequal pressures come from the tear narrowing a subclavian artery.
perOption.r3:c1: This reflects an enlarged, dissected thoracic aorta.
perOption.r3:c2: This reflects an enlarged, dissected thoracic aorta.
perOption.r3:c3: This reflects an enlarged, dissected thoracic aorta.
perOption.r4:c1: D-dimer rises with clot in PE and with blood in the false lumen in dissection.
perOption.r4:c2: D-dimer rises with clot in PE and with blood in the false lumen in dissection.
perOption.r4:c3: D-dimer rises with clot in PE and with blood in the false lumen in dissection.
perOption.r5:c1: ST elevation is the sign of STEMI; dissection can cause it only by involving a coronary artery.
perOption.r5:c2: ST elevation is the sign of STEMI; dissection can cause it only by involving a coronary artery.

questions.educationalObjective: Analyze cues to tell aortic dissection from MI and PE.

questions.stem: The CT angiogram shows a dissection starting in the ascending aorta. Complete the sentences by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: This is a {{b1}} dissection, which is treated with {{b2}}. Until then, the greatest threat to the client's life is {{b3}}.

options.text: a cardiac catheterization with a stent
aortic rupture or bleeding into the pericardium
an embolic stroke from atrial fibrillation

rationale.correct: Ascending aorta involvement makes it type A, which needs emergency surgery; rupture and tamponade are the immediate threats.

perOption.b1:a: Any dissection involving the ascending aorta is Stanford type A.
perOption.b1:b: Type B starts beyond the left subclavian artery.
perOption.b1:d: Lifting is a trigger with uncontrolled hypertension, not blunt trauma.
perOption.b2:a: Type A dissection is a surgical emergency because it can rupture or reach the heart.
perOption.b2:b: This is the usual treatment for uncomplicated type B.
perOption.b2:c: Thrombolysis would be fatal in a dissection.
perOption.b2:d: Coronary stenting does not treat the aorta.
perOption.b3:a: A type A tear can rupture or cause tamponade within minutes to hours.
perOption.b3:b: The client is in sinus rhythm.

questions.educationalObjective: Prioritize hypotheses in type A aortic dissection.

questions.stem: Review the prescriptions while the client waits for surgery. Select the 3 prescriptions the nurse should carry out first.

options.text: Esmolol infusion to a heart rate below 60/min
Nicardipine IV infusion after the heart rate is controlled
Heparin 80 units/kg IV bolus, then a continuous infusion
Aspirin 324 mg chewed now to limit clot formation
Hydralazine 10 mg IV push as the first drug given
0.9% sodium chloride 1 L bolus to protect the kidneys

rationale.correct: In dissection, control heart rate with a beta blocker first, then lower pressure with a vasodilator, and treat pain. Avoid anticoagulants and antiplatelets.

perOption.a: Beta blockade first lowers the force and rate of each beat, reducing shear on the aortic wall.
perOption.b: A vasodilator then lowers pressure to the target; given first it would cause reflex tachycardia.
perOption.c: Pain drives sympathetic tone, which raises pressure and heart rate.
perOption.d: Anticoagulation would worsen bleeding into the false lumen.
perOption.e: Antiplatelet drugs increase bleeding before aortic surgery.
perOption.f: A vasodilator alone causes reflex tachycardia, which increases shear on the aortic wall.
perOption.g: The client is hypertensive; fluid would raise pressure.

questions.educationalObjective: Generate solutions for type A aortic dissection before surgery.

exhibits.title: Prescriptions, 0010
exhibits.body: Esmolol infusion titrated to heart rate < 60/min. Nicardipine infusion titrated to systolic BP 100 to 120 mm Hg once heart rate is controlled. Morphine 4 mg IV every 2 hours as needed. Heparin bolus and infusion. Aspirin 324 mg. Hydralazine 10 mg IV. 0.9% sodium chloride 1 L bolus. Surgery at 0200.

questions.stem: Review the 0045 findings. Which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Notify the surgeon of the leg and urine changes now
Compare pulses, color and sensation in both legs
Continue the esmolol to keep the heart rate below 60/min
Increase IV fluids to raise urine output
Stop the nicardipine so the kidneys get more pressure
Give furosemide to increase urine output

rationale.correct: Signs of new organ or limb ischemia mean the dissection is extending; keep rate and pressure low, document the findings and get the surgeon now.

perOption.a: New leg numbness and low urine output mean the tear is extending into the iliac and renal arteries.
perOption.b: This documents the extent of new ischemia for the surgeon.
perOption.c: Rate and pressure control still slow the extension of the tear.
perOption.d: Low output here comes from a blocked renal artery, not low volume; raising pressure worsens the tear.
perOption.e: Allowing pressure to rise drives the dissection further.
perOption.f: A diuretic cannot help a kidney with no blood supply.

questions.educationalObjective: Take action when an aortic dissection extends.

questions.stem: The client had emergency repair with a graft. Review the findings on the first day after surgery. For each finding, indicate whether it is expected or needs follow-up.

rows.text: Systolic blood pressure 112 mm Hg on a nicardipine infusion
Chest tube drainage 60 mL/hour, serosanguineous
Unable to move or feel both legs
Urine output 15 mL/hour for 2 hours
Left pedal pulses 2+ and warm foot
Pain 4 of 10 with IV opioid

rationale.correct: Low pressure, modest drainage and restored leg perfusion are expected. Loss of leg movement and low urine output are serious complications of aortic repair.

perOption.r1:c1: After repair, pressure is kept low to protect the suture lines.
perOption.r1:c2: After repair, pressure is kept low to protect the suture lines.
perOption.r2:c1: Drainage under 100 mL/hour that is lightening in color is expected.
perOption.r2:c2: Drainage under 100 mL/hour that is lightening in color is expected.
perOption.r3:c1: Paraplegia after aortic surgery means spinal cord ischemia; it needs immediate action, such as spinal drainage.
perOption.r3:c2: Paraplegia after aortic surgery means spinal cord ischemia; it needs immediate action, such as spinal drainage.
perOption.r4:c1: Output below 0.5 mL/kg/hour suggests kidney injury from the dissection.
perOption.r4:c2: Output below 0.5 mL/kg/hour suggests kidney injury from the dissection.
perOption.r5:c1: Blood flow to the leg has been restored by the repair.
perOption.r5:c2: Blood flow to the leg has been restored by the repair.
perOption.r6:c1: Moderate pain after sternotomy is expected and controlled.
perOption.r6:c2: Moderate pain after sternotomy is expected and controlled.

rationale.correct: The cues are the bleeding, its cause (a warfarin interaction plus aspirin) and the mechanical valve that limits how anticoagulation is managed.

perOption.s2: A mechanical valve has a high clot risk, which affects how far anticoagulation can be reversed.
perOption.s4: This antibiotic strongly increases warfarin's effect.

perOption.s10: A proton pump inhibitor protects the stomach; not a problem here.

perOption.s14: Needed for dosing, but not a problem.

questions.educationalObjective: Recognize cues of warfarin-related bleeding.

questions.stem: For each finding, choose the explanation that fits best.

options.text: Vitamin K was absorbed from the diet
The aspirin dose raised the INR
Blood in the gut is digested and absorbed as protein
Acute blood loss, possibly not yet fully shown

rationale.correct: A drug interaction raised the INR, and the upper GI bleed explains the high BUN, falling hemoglobin and compensatory tachycardia.

perOption.b1:a: It inhibits CYP2C9, the enzyme that clears the more potent form of warfarin.
perOption.b1:b: Vitamin K would lower the INR.
perOption.b1:d: Aspirin affects platelets, not the INR.
perOption.b2:a: A high BUN with a normal creatinine is typical of upper GI bleeding.
perOption.b3:a: Hemoglobin falls further as fluid shifts into the vessels, so the loss may be greater than it appears.
perOption.b3:b: The fall from 12.8 in a month is too fast for this.
perOption.b4:a: Tachycardia keeps up output as volume falls.
perOption.b4:c: Pale, cool skin and low pressure show hypovolemia.

questions.educationalObjective: Analyze cues of over-anticoagulation and upper GI bleeding.

questions.stem: Complete the sentences by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: The client's most urgent problem is {{b1}}. Once the anticoagulation is reversed, the nurse must also watch for {{b2}} because {{b3}}.

options.text: a mechanical mitral valve has the highest clot risk
the INR is above the target range

rationale.correct: Treat the bleed first, but remember that full reversal in a client with a mechanical mitral valve brings a real risk of valve thrombosis and stroke.

perOption.b1:a: Ongoing bleeding with tachycardia and hypotension is the immediate threat.
perOption.b1:b: A minor problem compared with the bleed.
perOption.b1:c: There is no sign of fluid overload.
perOption.b2:a: Without anticoagulation, a mechanical valve can clot within days.
perOption.b2:b: The risk falls as anticoagulation is reversed.
perOption.b3:a: Mitral mechanical valves have a high clot risk, so anticoagulation must restart as soon as bleeding is controlled.
perOption.b3:b: This is what is being reversed.
perOption.b3:d: Age adds risk but is not the main reason.

questions.educationalObjective: Prioritize hypotheses in bleeding with a mechanical valve.

questions.stem: For each part of the plan, select the actions the nurse should anticipate. Each group has at least one answer.

options.text: Vitamin K 10 mg by slow IV infusion
Packed red blood cells as prescribed

rationale.correct: Reverse warfarin with IV vitamin K and PCC, restore volume with blood, and remove the causes: warfarin, aspirin and the interacting antibiotic.

perOption.a: IV vitamin K starts working in hours and lasts.
perOption.b: PCC replaces clotting factors within minutes for major bleeding.
perOption.f: Hemoglobin 7.9 with active bleeding needs transfusion.
perOption.g: Dextrose in water leaves the vessels and does not restore volume.
perOption.h: Warfarin is held until bleeding is controlled and the plan is reviewed.
perOption.i: Removes the interaction that raised the INR.
perOption.j: Acid suppression stabilizes clots on a peptic ulcer.
perOption.k: Aspirin adds to bleeding and is held.

exhibits.title: Prescriptions, 1330
exhibits.body: Vitamin K 10 mg IV over 30 minutes. Four-factor PCC 50 units/kg IV. Type and crossmatch 2 units of packed red blood cells. Pantoprazole 80 mg IV. Hold warfarin and aspirin. Stop trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole; start an alternative antibiotic. Gastroenterology consult for endoscopy.

questions.stem: The prescription is four-factor prothrombin complex concentrate 50 units/kg IV. The client weighs 165 lb. How many units should the nurse prepare? Record your answer as a whole number.

rationale.correct: 165 lb divided by 2.2 = 75 kg. 75 kg x 50 units/kg = 3,750 units, which is below the usual maximum of 5,000 units.

questions.educationalObjective: Recognize cues of heparin-induced thrombocytopenia.

questions.stem: For each statement about the client, indicate whether it is accurate or inaccurate.

rows.text: The low platelet count puts the client at high risk of bleeding.
The timing, 7 days after heparin started, fits HIT.
The cold left foot may be caused by an arterial clot linked to HIT.
The heparin flushes are too small to matter.
Switching to enoxaparin would be a safe alternative.

rationale.correct: HIT is an immune clotting disorder: the low platelets are a sign, not the danger, and all heparins must stop.

perOption.r1:c1: In HIT, antibodies activate platelets, so the main danger is clotting, not bleeding.
perOption.r1:c2: In HIT, antibodies activate platelets, so the main danger is clotting, not bleeding.
perOption.r2:c1: HIT usually appears 5 to 10 days after first exposure.
perOption.r2:c2: HIT usually appears 5 to 10 days after first exposure.
perOption.r3:c1: HIT causes venous and arterial thrombosis.
perOption.r3:c2: HIT causes venous and arterial thrombosis.
perOption.r4:c1: Any heparin, even flushes, keeps the reaction going.
perOption.r4:c2: Any heparin, even flushes, keeps the reaction going.

questions.stem: Which prescriptions should the nurse anticipate for this client? Select all that apply.

options.text: Replace heparin flushes with 0.9% sodium chloride flushes
Switch to enoxaparin 1 mg/kg every 12 hours

rationale.correct: Stop every heparin source, start a non-heparin anticoagulant and confirm the diagnosis; avoid platelets, LMWH and early warfarin.

perOption.b: Hidden heparin sources must also stop.
perOption.c: A direct thrombin inhibitor anticoagulates without heparin; with normal liver function argatroban is suitable.

perOption.g: Warfarin is started only after platelets recover, because early warfarin can cause venous limb gangrene in HIT.

exhibits.title: Prescriptions, 0900
exhibits.body: Vascular surgery consult for the left leg. Hematology consult. The provider asks the nurse to review the anticoagulation plan with pharmacy.

questions.stem: Argatroban is prescribed at 2 mcg/kg/minute. The bag contains argatroban 250 mg in 250 mL. The client weighs 80 kg. At what rate should the nurse set the pump? Record your answer to one decimal place.

rationale.correct: 2 mcg/kg/min x 80 kg = 160 mcg/min. 160 mcg/min x 60 = 9,600 mcg/hour = 9.6 mg/hour. The bag is 1 mg/mL, so the rate is 9.6 mL/hour.

questions.stem: Highlight the findings that require immediate follow-up.

rationale.correct: Sudden fall in chest tube drainage, falling pressure with a narrow pulse pressure, rising CVP and pulsus paradoxus are the cues of tamponade.

perOption.r1: A sudden stop after heavy drainage suggests clotted tubes, so blood is collecting around the heart.
perOption.r2: Falling systolic pressure with a narrowing pulse pressure (50 to 16 mm Hg) shows falling stroke volume.
perOption.r3: Rising filling pressure with falling output suggests compression of the heart.
perOption.r4: Pulsus paradoxus above 10 mm Hg is a sign of tamponade.
perOption.r6: Common after bypass; not a finding in itself.

questions.educationalObjective: Recognize cues of cardiac tamponade after cardiac surgery.

questions.stem: Complete the sentences by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: The sudden drop in chest tube drainage most likely means {{b1}}. The rising CVP with falling blood pressure shows that {{b2}}. The distended neck veins and muffled heart sounds with low blood pressure are known as {{b3}}.

options.text: clot is blocking the tubes while bleeding continues
the suction is set too high
the heart cannot fill because it is compressed
the client is fluid overloaded from surgery
the client is vasodilated from nitroglycerin

rationale.correct: Blocked tubes with continued bleeding cause tamponade, which stops the heart from filling.

perOption.b1:a: Bleeding has not stopped; blood is now trapped in the mediastinum.
perOption.b1:b: Falling pressure and rising CVP argue against this.
perOption.b2:a: Pressure in the pericardium stops the ventricles filling, so CVP rises while output falls.
perOption.b2:b: Overload would not cause falling pressure with falling drainage.
perOption.b2:c: Graft failure causes ischemia on the ECG and does not explain falling drainage.
perOption.b3:a: Hypotension, distended neck veins and muffled heart sounds.
perOption.b3:b: That is hypertension, bradycardia and irregular breathing with raised ICP.
perOption.b3:c: That describes risk factors for clotting.

questions.educationalObjective: Analyze cues of postoperative cardiac tamponade.

questions.stem: Complete the diagram by choosing the condition the client is most likely experiencing, 2 actions the nurse should take, and 2 parameters the nurse should monitor.

actions.text: Call the cardiac surgeon to the bedside now
Give furosemide for the raised CVP
Raise the nitroglycerin to treat ischemia

parameters.text: Bowel sounds in all four quadrants

rationale.correct: Tamponade after cardiac surgery is a surgical emergency: call the surgeon and prepare for reopening while tracking pressure and CVP.

perOption.c1: Beck's triad, pulsus paradoxus and blocked chest tubes after surgery.
perOption.c2: Hypovolemia lowers CVP; here it is rising.
perOption.c3: Possible after surgery, but tracheal shift and absent breath sounds are not reported.
perOption.c4: This would show new ischemia on the ECG.
perOption.a1: Tamponade after surgery needs reopening or drainage.
perOption.a2: Emergency sternotomy may be done in the ICU.
perOption.a3: Diuresis lowers preload, which the compressed heart depends on.
perOption.a5: This would not relieve the compression.
perOption.p1: Show the effect of compression on stroke volume.
perOption.p2: Rising CVP tracks rising pericardial pressure.

questions.educationalObjective: Prioritize care in postoperative cardiac tamponade.

questions.stem: While the surgeon is on the way, the nurse reviews the client's infusions and standing prescriptions. For each, indicate whether the nurse should continue it, stop it, or start it.

rows.text: Nitroglycerin infusion
0.9% sodium chloride bolus as prescribed for hypotension
Furosemide 20 mg IV scheduled for 0200
Morphine 4 mg IV for restlessness
Type and crossmatch, 2 units ready

rationale.correct: Stop drugs that lower preload or pressure, support preload with fluid and prepare blood.

perOption.r1:c1: A vasodilator lowers preload and pressure; the compressed heart needs both.
perOption.r1:c2: A vasodilator lowers preload and pressure; the compressed heart needs both.
perOption.r2:c1: Raising preload can briefly support output until the pericardium is drained.
perOption.r2:c2: Raising preload can briefly support output until the pericardium is drained.
perOption.r4:c1: Restlessness is a sign of poor perfusion; morphine also vasodilates and can hide it.
perOption.r4:c2: Restlessness is a sign of poor perfusion; morphine also vasodilates and can hide it.
perOption.r5:c1: Bleeding continues and reopening is likely.
perOption.r5:c2: Bleeding continues and reopening is likely.

questions.educationalObjective: Generate solutions while awaiting surgical treatment of tamponade.

exhibits.title: Infusions and prescriptions, 0205
exhibits.body: Nitroglycerin 10 mcg/minute. 0.9% sodium chloride 250 mL bolus for SBP < 90 mm Hg. Furosemide 20 mg IV at 0200. Morphine 4 mg IV every 2 hours as needed. Type and crossmatch 2 units.

questions.stem: At 0210 the monitor shows a narrow-complex rhythm at 118/min, and no pulse can be felt. The surgeon is 3 minutes away. Which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Call for help and start the cardiac surgery arrest protocol
Prepare the chest-opening tray for emergency resternotomy
Start compressions if the chest cannot be opened within a minute
Deliver an unsynchronized shock at 200 joules right away
Wait for the surgeon to arrive before starting resuscitation
Give furosemide 40 mg IV to bring the high CVP down

rationale.correct: Pulseless electrical activity from tamponade after cardiac surgery needs emergency reopening, with compressions only as a bridge.

perOption.a: Pulseless electrical activity after cardiac surgery is treated by protocol while the team prepares to reopen.
perOption.b: Reopening relieves tamponade, the cause of the arrest; it should happen within about 5 minutes.
perOption.c: Compressions maintain some perfusion until the chest can be opened.
perOption.d: A vasodilator lowers the preload and pressure the compressed heart depends on.
perOption.e: PEA is not a shockable rhythm; shocks treat VF and pulseless VT.
perOption.f: Every minute without perfusion worsens the outcome; the protocol starts at once.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
American Heart Association Guidelines for CPR and Emergency Cardiovascular Care

questions.educationalObjective: Take action for arrest from tamponade after cardiac surgery.

questions.stem: Clot was removed from around the heart at the bedside and a bleeding graft site was repaired. Review the 0500 findings. For each finding, indicate whether it shows the treatment worked or needs follow-up.

rows.text: Blood pressure 116/70 mm Hg, pulse pressure 46 mm Hg
CVP 7 mm Hg
Chest tube drainage 60 mL/hour, lightening in color
Urine output 55 mL/hour
Systolic fall on inspiration of 16 mm Hg
Client follows commands and moves all four limbs

rationale.correct: Recovered pressure, falling CVP, steady drainage and good urine output show success; persistent pulsus paradoxus needs reporting.

perOption.r2:c1: Filling pressure has fallen as the compression is relieved.
perOption.r2:c2: Filling pressure has fallen as the compression is relieved.
perOption.r5:c1: Pulsus paradoxus that persists suggests continuing pericardial compression.
perOption.r5:c2: Pulsus paradoxus that persists suggests continuing pericardial compression.
perOption.r6:c1: Neurologic function is intact after the arrest.
perOption.r6:c2: Neurologic function is intact after the arrest.

questions.educationalObjective: Evaluate outcomes after relief of cardiac tamponade.

exhibits.title: Emergency department, 2340
exhibits.body: A 58-year-old client had sudden, severe chest pain that "tore" through to the back between the shoulder blades while lifting a heavy box. History: poorly controlled hypertension; the client stopped amlodipine 3 months ago. The client is pale, sweating and anxious. A new soft diastolic murmur is heard at the left sternal border. The right radial pulse is stronger than the left. The chest x-ray shows a widened mediastinum. The ECG shows sinus tachycardia without ST elevation.

caseStudies.title: Warfarin over-anticoagulation with a GI bleed and a mechanical valve

exhibits.title: Emergency department, 1300
exhibits.body: A 72-year-old client with a mechanical mitral valve has taken warfarin 5 mg daily for 6 years. Seven days ago, a clinic started trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole for a urinary tract infection. Since yesterday, the client has had black, tarry stools and dizziness when standing. The client also takes aspirin 81 mg daily and omeprazole. Skin is pale and cool. Weight 165 lb (75 kg).

exhibits.title: Medical unit, day 7, 0800
exhibits.body: A 66-year-old client was admitted 7 days ago with a right femoral deep vein thrombosis and started on a heparin infusion. Today the client reports that the left foot is cold and painful. The left foot is pale and cool with a weak dorsalis pedis pulse; the right leg is less swollen than on admission. The client also has a red, painful patch on the abdomen where heparin was given before the infusion started. Weight 80 kg. Liver function is normal.

rows.label: aPTT
cells: 25 to 35 s; target 60 to 90 s on heparin

exhibits.title: Medication record
exhibits.body: Heparin infusion by protocol. Heparin 10 units/mL flush to the PICC line every 8 hours. Docusate 100 mg twice daily. Acetaminophen 650 mg every 6 hours as needed.

caseStudies.title: Cardiac tamponade after coronary bypass surgery

exhibits.title: Cardiac surgery ICU, 0200
exhibits.body: A 64-year-old client is 6 hours after coronary artery bypass grafting. The client is extubated, on a low-dose nitroglycerin infusion, with mediastinal chest tubes to suction and temporary epicardial pacing wires. At 0200 the client is restless and says, "I can't get comfortable." Neck veins are distended with the head of the bed at 30 degrees. Heart sounds are hard to hear. The systolic pressure falls 18 mm Hg on inspiration.

testSets.title: NCLEX-RN adaptive exam
testSets.description: Works like the real NCLEX-RN: each question depends on your answers so far, and the exam stops once your result is clear, after 85 to 150 questions. Choose timed (5 hours) or untimed. No going back; answers and rationales at the end. The questions are being rewritten to real NCLEX difficulty and recalibrated, so treat your result as a practice estimate.
